title: Which is easier to balance, a pencil or a broom? Broom flat at 1.50 s, pencil 0.53 s, 2.83x: root 8
description:
Which is easier to balance, a pencil or a broom? Two panels on the same clock: a uniform thin stick stands on a fingertip with its foot held in place (a hinge: the foot neither slips nor lifts) and is let go from rest 1 degree off vertical; theta is measured from vertical. About the foot I = m L^2 / 3 and the torque is m g (L / 2) sin theta, so theta'' = (3 g / (2 L)) sin theta and the mass cancels; the energy form is theta'^2 = (3 g / L)(cos theta0 - cos theta). Top panel: the broom, L = 1.2 m. Bottom panel: the pencil, L = 0.15 m, 8 times shorter, drawn 8x so both sticks are the same length on screen. g = 9.80665 m/s^2. The stick lies flat at theta = 90 degrees. Both are integrated by RK4 at 10000 steps per second (dt = 1e-04 s) with the floor and the 45-degree crossing located by bisection inside the step, checked against the energy form at every step, against the quadrature of the energy form, against sqrt(8) for the time ratio, and by a half-step rerun. Shown at 1/3 speed; the drop repeats every 8 s of video, 5 drops in 40 s. Deterministic, no seed.

Measured:
- the broom (1.2 m) lies flat at 1.4985 s and passes 45 degrees at 1.2889 s (quadrature of the energy form 1.4985 s and 1.2889 s); at the floor theta' = 4.9510 rad/s (energy form sqrt(3 g cos theta0 / L) = 4.9510) and the tip comes down at 5.94 m/s
- the pencil (0.15 m) lies flat at 0.5298 s and passes 45 degrees at 0.4557 s (quadrature 0.5298 s and 0.4557 s); at the floor theta' = 14.0037 rad/s (energy form 14.0037) and the tip comes down at 2.10 m/s
- the ratio of the flat times is 2.82843 = sqrt(8) = 2.82843 (diff -2.1e-14), and the ratio of the 45-degree times is 2.82843 too: in the scaled time tau = t sqrt(3 g / (2 L)) the equation is theta'' = sin theta for every length, so every time in the fall scales with sqrt(L); the pencil's fall is the broom's fall played 2.8284 times faster
- small-angle growth rate sqrt(3 g / (2 L)) = 3.5012 per second for the broom (e-fold 0.2856 s; the growing mode doubles every 0.1980 s; from rest the lean follows cosh and first doubles at 0.3761 s: RK4 2 degrees at 0.3762 s, 4 degrees at 0.5894 s, 10 degrees at 0.8551 s) against 9.9029 per second for the pencil (e-fold 0.1010 s; 2 degrees at 0.1330 s, 10 degrees at 0.3023 s)
- the foot's push on the stick (in weights, the same curve for both sticks): vertical 0.9998 and horizontal +0.0131 at the release; the forward push peaks at +0.229 at 26.7 degrees and reverses at 48.2 degrees (cos theta = 2/3); the vertical push falls to 0.0001 at 70.5 degrees (closed form (3 cos theta - 1)^2 / 4, zero at cos theta = 1/3) and is 0.2500 at the floor; the pull back toward the foot grows late in the fall to 1.4998 weights at the floor ((3/2) cos theta0); the sideways push exceeds the vertical push from 54.1 degrees on, so a foot on a plain floor would slip: it must be held
- the broom from other leans: 0.5 degrees flat at 1.6964 s, 2 degrees at 1.3005 s, 5 degrees at 1.0390 s
- other lengths from 1 degree: a 30 cm ruler is flat at 0.7492 s (exactly half the broom's time, sqrt(0.3 / 1.2) = 0.5000), a 1 m stick at 1.3679 s, a 10 cm stub at 0.4326 s, a 4.8 m pole at 2.9969 s (exactly twice, sqrt(4.8 / 1.2) = 2.0000)
- checks: theta'^2 stays within 2.6e-13 rad^2/s^2 (broom) and 2.2e-12 (pencil) of the energy form and the energy drifts by 1.1e-14 of the energy released; RK4 and the quadrature agree within 9.2e-14 s (broom) and 2.9e-14 s (pencil); the half-step rerun (20000 steps per second) moves the flat times by -8.9e-16 s and -3.4e-15 s and the ratio stays 2.828427

Why: the stick tips because gravity's torque about the foot, m g (L / 2) sin theta, grows with the lean while the resistance to turning, I = m L^2 / 3, grows with the square of the length. The angular acceleration is (3 g / (2 L)) sin theta: the longer the stick, the slower the lean grows, with a time scale sqrt(2 L / (3 g)). The mass cancels, so a heavy broom and a light one fall alike. Make the stick 8 times as long and every moment of the fall takes sqrt(8) = 2.83 times longer: 1.50 s for the broom against 0.53 s for the pencil. That is why the broom is the easier one to balance: your hand has nearly three times as long to catch the same lean.

Rerun sims/broom/broom.py with projects/broom/manifest.json and you get these numbers exactly.
